THE FRAME'S SOUND. THE OLD CLOTH PANELS AREN'T. WE
NEED FABRIC AND CLIPS.
pages.raw_text: The frame’s sound. The old cloth panels aren’t. We need fabric and clips.

pages.text: I CAN HELP.
pages.raw_text: I can help.

pages.text: HELP ME DO YOUR JOB, OR ASK ME TO DO MINE?
pages.raw_text: Help me do your job, or ask me to do mine?

pages.text:
TONIGHT'S STYLING. A TRIAL. WE CAN DISCUSS FUTURE
WORK AFTER WE'VE TRIED WORKING TOGETHER.
pages.raw_text: Tonight’s styling. A trial. We can discuss future work after we’ve tried working together.

pages.text: GOOD. TONIGHT, AND MY EQUIPMENT COMES BACK.
pages.raw_text: Good. Tonight, and my equipment comes back.

pages.text: YOUR EQUIPMENT COMES BACK.
pages.raw_text: Your equipment comes back.

pages.text:
I'D LIKE TO WORK WITH YOU TONIGHT. LET'S SEE HOW
THE TRIAL GOES.
pages.raw_text: I’d like to work with you tonight. Let’s see how the trial goes.

pages.text: A CLEAR BRIEF. I FIND THOSE VERY ATTRACTIVE.
pages.raw_text: A clear brief. I find those very attractive.

pages.text: PROFESSIONALLY.
pages.raw_text: Professionally.

pages.text: AT THE MOMENT, WE'RE DISCUSSING A SCREEN.
pages.raw_text: At the moment, we’re discussing a screen.

pages.text:
I'D ENJOY DOING THIS WITH YOU. TONIGHT'S STYLING,
WITH YOUR EQUIPMENT RETURNED.
pages.raw_text: I’d enjoy doing this with you. Tonight’s styling, with your equipment returned.

pages.text: SO WOULD I. WE'LL MAKE THE ROOM USABLE.
pages.raw_text: So would I. We’ll make the room usable.

pages.text: SO NOBODY NOTICES THE STYLING.
pages.raw_text: So nobody notices the styling.

pages.text: I DIDN'T SAY INVISIBLE, JACKIE.
pages.raw_text: I didn’t say invisible, Jackie.

pages.text:
I'D LIKE YOUR HELP TONIGHT. AND I'D LIKE TO SEE
YOU PERSONALLY. I'M TRYING TO ASK THOSE IN
SEPARATE VOICES.
pages.raw_text: I’d like your help tonight. And I’d like to see you personally. I’m trying to ask those in separate voices.

pages.text:
GOOD. IF YOU ASK ME OUT, TRY NOT TO OPEN WITH
"DOES THIS FOLD?"
pages.raw_text: Good. If you ask me out, try not to open with “Does this fold?”

pages.text:
THE PERSONAL INVITATION IS SEPARATE FROM TONIGHT'S
WORK.
pages.raw_text: The personal invitation is separate from tonight’s work.

pages.text:
THEN LET'S DO THE WORK. WE CAN TALK ABOUT THE
INVITATION SEPARATELY.
pages.raw_text: Then let’s do the work. We can talk about the invitation separately.

LIDDED POT WAITING IN THE KITCHEN.

speech.raw_text: The frame’s sound. The old cloth panels aren’t. We need fabric and clips.
I can help.
Help me do your job, or ask me to do mine?
Tonight’s styling. A trial. We can discuss future work after we’ve tried working together.
Good. Tonight, and my equipment comes back.
Your equipment comes back.
A clear brief. I find those very attractive.
Professionally.
At the moment, we’re discussing a screen.
So would I. We’ll make the room usable.
So nobody notices the styling.
I didn’t say invisible, Jackie.
Good. If you ask me out, try not to open with “Does this fold?”
The personal invitation is separate from tonight’s work.
Then let’s do the work. We can talk about the invitation separately.
A solid frame. It needs cloth panels to provide privacy. The frame alone leaves very little to the imagination.
Pairs of dots on the upper rail. The drawing puts the clips there and leaves the bottom clear.
Vivian’s model has an arriving visitor, Rita’s display and the kitchen hatch, with two sightlines. Hide the display; leave the hatch
visible. Dinner is the part of my evening I want inspected.
A cardboard arriving guest marks the start of the sightline. No opinions, no dietary announcements. I may ask Vivian to leave it.
The sample layout’s stand-in for Rita’s covered display. The arrival view needs to stop before it gets here.
Push this little screen around Vivian’s sample layout to see which of the two sightlines it blocks. Very considerate of her to make my
mistakes small.
There’s a clean spare sheet in the kitchen. You can use it.
For Vivian’s screen.
Good. I didn’t want to be the last person to know what the sheets were doing.
The spare sheet. Frankie said it’s available.
Large laundry clips. They’ll hold the sheet at the paired dots on the upper rail. I knew all that laundry was preparing me for glamour.
The sheet lies over the upper rail, with the bottom clear of the floor. Now it needs clipping.
Clips at the dots, lower edge clear. Taut enough to hang cleanly, loose enough to fold.
That looks expensive.
You’re welcome.
That puts the cloth across people’s feet.
It did look rather secure.
To the people. Drape it over the upper rail, then clip at the dots.
You’ve hidden the kitchen hatch. We’re concealing Rita’s surprise, not protecting people from the sight of dinner.
I’ll move the screen and leave the hatch visible.
That’s the position. Arrivals can’t see the display; the kitchen hatch stays in view.
Rita gets her surprise, and I get seen cooking.
Both temperaments catered for. I’ll mark it on the courtyard plan.
With you there, who’ll be looking at the screen?
Quite a few people. I’m very good.
Now: what job are we agreeing to, and how are we making the screen stand?
There’s an industry mixer tonight. I could take you. People you’d want to meet.
That sounds very tempting.
It is. I’m good at invitations.
Another occasion, then.
You’re not disappointed?
A little. But keep your promise here. The mixer will survive without us. Everyone there is very good at explaining why someone important hasn’t
arrived.
Fair. Supper first; afterward stays a possibility.
If we manage it, I’ll be the one still smelling faintly of onions.
The screen’s yours for tonight. We’ve agreed the job; the layout works.
Thank you. I’ll get your equipment back to you.
Good. Let’s put it in the courtyard.
Six full suppers, or eight tasting bowls using the method in the margin.
What’s a tasting bowl?
A small portion with eye contact.
Including one for you. I won’t have you watching me chew while you explain what I’m tasting.
Eight bowls. One of them mine. I’ll follow the margin’s method.
My six-full-supper recipe, with the eight-tasting-bowl method written in the margin. Smaller portions, larger adjectives. I may be
moving up in the world.
A pot with a proper lid. Cook the hotpot here, then keep it lidded in the kitchen until it’s time to carry it.
A lid that fits the pot. There’s a reason neither of us is serving supper off the floor.
On to cook the base and vegetables. Off before the herbs. A cook should know when to stop helping.
The bean-and-tomato base is in the pot.
Right to the eight-bowl mark. Tasting portions for all eight of us.
The measured stock is in. The base and stock can go in either order; the vegetables follow the base.
Vegetables in. The cooking comes before the fresh finish.
Base, stock, vegetables. A short cook, and the hotpot is ready for its fresh finish.
Heat off. Now the herbs.
Herbs in after cooking, with the heat off. A fresh finish, not boiled perfume.
Lid on. Eight tasting portions, ready for later.
My recipe says to turn the heat off before adding the herbs. Apparently I wrote it for a man I don’t trust.
Heat off first. I’ll keep the herbs for then.
That’s stock for six, and there are eight of us. I can make a tasting portion elegant; I can’t make two people disappear. Refill the jug to the
eight-tasting-bowl mark shown in the recipe’s margin.
The hotpot is finished, but it needs its lid before it travels. I’d like the courtyard to smell of supper without wearing it.
Oh, Jackie. Thinking about all the lovely things Rita’s offering us...
It’s the onion.
Oh. I was one hug away from putting my sleeve in the beans.
I am grateful to her, though.
I know.
Ready for eight tasting bowls. The lid stays on, and it waits here until we serve.
